title: Single-User to Multi-User SIM-AC-CPA Security
summary: Whether single-user security lifts to the multi-user SIM-AC-CPA notion remains open; simulator-state inconsistencies block the hybrid proof, while only strengthened SIM*-AC definitions are covered.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether single-user SIM-AC-CPA security implies multi-user SIM-AC-CPA security. A hybrid proof of this implication is obstructed by inconsistencies in simulator state between hybrid steps. A follow-up result establishes that the hybrid argument works for strengthened $\mathrm{SIM}^{*}\text{-}\mathrm{AC}$ definitions, but this only partially resolves the question and does not establish the implication for the original SIM-AC-CPA notion.

scope.domain: Simulation-based security for practical encryption schemes under adaptive compromise.
parameters: security definition: original SIM-AC-CPA versus strengthened SIM*-AC
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether single-user SIM-AC-CPA security implies multi-user SIM-AC-CPA security under the original notion.

citations.label: Handling Adaptive Compromise for Practical Encryption Schemes

progress.summary: The source explicitly leaves the single-user-to-multi-user implication open because a hybrid proof must manage inconsistent simulator state between hybrid steps. A follow-up result handles strengthened SIM*-AC definitions only, so the original implication remains unresolved.
citation_labels: Joseph Jaeger et al., Handling Adaptive Compromise for Practical Encryption Schemes
